resources.string: With the phone closed, hold a volume button to open the outside-screen page (or switch the flashlight) you chose for it in LCD Clock; at first volume-down opens the timer and volume-up your Home Assistant buttons. Short presses still change the volume, and nothing happens while the phone is open. While you close the phone it also turns a picture-in-picture window back into its full app, so the video keeps playing, and the first time a playing video goes into picture-in-picture after a fold it turns the screen once so the window doesn\'t land off-screen; for that it watches which app is in front (if that\'s switched on in LCD Clock).
This phone has no sound picker.

Swipe up on the clock face. Tap one to read all of it on its own page; dismiss one with ×, or CLEAR them all. While the phone is locked they\'re restricted (just the app and its lock-screen text, whatever your lock screen is set to show); unlock with the fingerprint to see the rest.

Swipe down on the clock face. Choose and order the controls below. Hold SOS for 3 seconds to start it: ··· ——— ··· with the flashlight, vibration and a loud beep at full alarm volume, until tapped again, even with the screen off or the phone locked. BEDTIME switches Digital Wellbeing\'s Bedtime mode on and off. Home Assistant and VPN work only while the phone is unlocked: tapping one while locked asks for your fingerprint, then switches it. Android doesn\'t let apps switch Wi-Fi, mobile data or Bluetooth.
With the phone closed and the outside screen on, hold a volume button for a moment to jump straight to a page, or to switch the flashlight. Short presses still change the volume.

Battery saver and Night Light need a permission Android only gives from a computer, once: with the phone connected over USB debugging, run\nadb shell pm grant dev.lcdclock android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

For the recorder (and other apps\' recordings in Recordings), calendar and weather pages, and the timer\'s notification.
In the order you swipe through them on the outside screen, after the clock face. Each has its own screen timeout.

LCD Clock\'s own copy of the face, put up when the outside screen wakes: swipe left or right for the pages, up or down for Motorola\'s face, panels and notifications. The padlock above the alarm bell is lit while the phone is locked; touch the fingerprint sensor to unlock, as on Motorola\'s face.

Close the phone while one of these is still running, even from Recents, and the cover button stays off until you next open it, so the banking app doesn\'t see an accessibility service come on. The cover pages and volume holds wait until then too, and a video playing doesn\'t switch it on while one is running. Swipe the banking app away from Recents when you\'ve finished to have them back.
Needs usage access, to see when a banking app was used.
To tell when a banking app has been swiped away, LCD Clock needs a permission only a computer can grant: run ./install.sh again. Until then, only a banking app in front when the phone closes counts.
Keep playing when you close the phone

The razr closes picture-in-picture windows the moment it folds, and apps stop their video when that happens. With this on, LCD Clock turns the window back into the full app while the phone is closing, so apps that can play in the background (YouTube, Twitch) keep the sound going. Open the phone and the app is there full screen, still playing. The razr also loses track of where picture-in-picture belongs whenever it folds, which sends the next window off the right edge of the screen; to put that right the screen turns once (a moment of black) the first time a playing video leaves the screen after the phone has been folded. Needs the cover button (accessibility) turned on. While the phone is open, this keeps the cover button on whenever a video app is playing, so a banking app opened then may object; switch this off if that matters. A video started while a banking app is still running doesn\'t switch it on.

string-array.item: LCD Clock\'s own countdown timer: it keeps running with the screen off and rings on the outside screen.

A daily alarm: tap the bell to turn it on or off. SNOOZE puts it off for the time chosen below; until it rings again the bell blinks, on the face too, and tapping the blinking bell cancels the snooze (the alarm stays on for tomorrow).
Your events for the next 7 days.
The forecast for your approximate location, from Open-Meteo.
LCD Clock\'s own recorder: records even with the screen off and the phone locked, saving to Recordings. Playing and LIST (every recording in Recordings) need the phone unlocked.

Your Home Assistant buttons. Set up its buttons below; it shows once one is set up. The buttons work only while the phone is unlocked: tapping one while locked asks for your fingerprint, then switches it.
A tab per app with music, showing the app\'s icon. Opens when music starts.

Three icon buttons on the outside screen\'s HOME page (a volume hold can open it; see Volume button holds). Each button runs its Home Assistant actions using the Home Assistant app\'s own login; add two actions to one button to toggle two things at once.

With a long-lived access token (Home Assistant → your profile → Security), each HOME icon lights while any of its entities is on, and tapping switches them all off, or all on. The server needs an https:// address, so the token is never sent unencrypted. Buttons without entities keep using their widget actions.
